newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends little changed vs US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends little changed vs US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed little changed at 8.2931 on Monday from last Friday's 8.2932 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai despite a heavy foreign trade surplus for January to May announced late last week, traders said.
The weighted average price on Friday was 8.2930.

Official figures issued after trading closed on Friday put China's foreign trade surplus for the first five months of the year at $13.95 billion against a deficit of $451 million in the same period last year.
Traders said the market had expected the strong surplus and that the news had largely been digested.

The yuan opened down at an intraday low of 8.2934 and rose slightly to move around the 8.2930 level for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.2924. Trading was dull with most business done at 8.2928, traders said.
"The news about the strong foreign trade surplus had been expected," one trader said. "Its impact on the market today was limited as a result."
A second dealer said market sentiment was cautious after the central bank, the People's Bank, intervened to depress the yuan earlier this month.
"Cautious sentiment dominated the market today, making the yuan move in a narrow range," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move around the 8.2930 level on Tuesday.
The yuan closed down at an intraday low of 7.3000 from 7.2500 against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0709 from 1.0725 against the Hong Kong dollar.
